title: Sterile-network deployment discovery - Sentinel Labs intake
summary: Initial discovery for a fully air-isolated inference deployment inside Sentinel Labs' sterile network. Key constraints: no outbound internet, HSM-backed KMS requirement, restricted update windows, legacy NVIDIA GPU fleet (two x A40s per rack initially), strict audit/retention needs. Discussed Redwood Private options, update mechanics for air-gapped sites, acceptance criteria and footprint estimation. Agreed next step: architecture workshop + on-site hw validation + security packet share.
topics: deployment topology options (private vs dedicated vs hosted)
hardware constraints and sizing (A40 vs A100)
compliance needs: SOC2/ISO, audit logs, SSO/SAML and RBAC
telemetry and observability in isolated networks
action_items: Arielle: Send Private deployment security packet (SOC2, network checklist, KMS integration notes) by 2027-03-25
Marco: Draft initial sizing estimate (2 A40 per node baseline) and rough cost delta for A100 option by 2027-03-28
Luis: Share current rack power/cooling spec and existing GPU inventory by 2027-03-24
Tess: Provide regulatory retention window and audit evidence requirements (retention periods) by 2027-03-29
next_steps: Schedule on-site HW validation visit (tentative week of 2027-04-11)
Run architecture workshop with infra + security (60-90m) — Redwood to propose times
Set up a short pilot proposal doc + pricing for sealed-network private deployment
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-03-22 14:00 PST; Duration: ~47m; Attendees: Arielle Chen, Marco Alvarez, Priya Nair (Redwood) -- Dr. Kavita Rao, Luis Mendes, Tess Monroe, Raj Patel (Sentinel Labs)

Summary (auto): intake call for fully isolated inference node; primary drivers are data residency/regulatory, zero egress, HSM/KMS integration, predictable latency for triage workflows.

00:00 Arielle Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:06 Dr. Kavita Rao: Yes, loud and clear. Thanks for taking the time.
00:09 Arielle Chen: Quick intros — I'm Arielle, AE on the account, Marco is our SE focusing on private deployments, Priya helps with solutions.
00:20 Marco Alvarez: Hey all. We'll try to keep it technical but also cover compliance needs.
00:25 Luis Mendes: Thanks. I'll give an overview of our environment — just to set context: we run a sterile network, physically isolated, no outbound connectivity, strict egress controls.
00:36 Arielle Chen: Understood. When you say physically isolated, do you mean no internet at all or limited whitelisted proxies?
00:41 Luis Mendes: No internet. Period. We have an air-gapped enclave inside the facility. Updates are via vetted USB media or physically carried images.
00:49 Marco Alvarez: Ok that's important — our private deployment supports air-gap workflows, but the mechanics vary. We typically deliver a signed image and an update bundle that your ops team can ingestion offline.
00:59 Tess Monroe: When you say "signed image", what about key management? We require HSM-backed keys for signing and for any KMS operations.
01:05 Marco Alvarez: We can integrate with on-prem HSMs — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS via PKCS#11-compatible HSMs, and we have patterns for pulling keys locally while keeping control plane isolated.
01:18 Tess Monroe: Are those integrations pre-built or is that custom work?
01:21 Priya Nair: We have documented integrations — most customers require a short integration project for cert provisioning and rotate keys. We'll share the integration checklist.
01:30 Dr. Kavita Rao: Our model registry and data never leave the lab. We need to ensure model versions and prompts are auditable. Can Redwood provide immutable audit logs?
01:38 Marco Alvarez: Yes — audit logs are part of the Private console. In an air-gapped setup we run a local control-plane replica that writes logs to your internal ELK/Syslog. There may be small differences vs hosted bc we can't ship telemetry out, but audit integrity stays.
01:54 Raj Patel: Just flagging — our current GPU fleet is older: mostly A40 cards in two-rack cages, and per-rack power is ~12kW. We're exploring whether we need A100s for throughput.
02:06 Marco Alvarez: A40s can run many model families but you'll see throughput limits vs A100/H100. For retrieval and triage workloads with short context, A40 may be fine. For larger context or high throughput, we'd recommend A100 or quantized LLMs. We'll sketch perf numbers.
02:23 Luis Mendes: Also important: patch windows. We can only allow updates monthly, and security team inspects images physically. How do you handle patching and CVEs for an offline deployment?
02:33 Marco Alvarez: We produce patch bundles with CVE notes and a verifiable signature. Your team validates signatures before applying. We can also provide backported security fixes in the bundle.
02:42 Tess Monroe: What about telemetry — we rely on observability for SLA checks. In an isolated environment we can't transmit telemetry. Do you recommend a local observability stack?
02:50 Priya Nair: Yes, most customers deploy a local Prometheus/Grafana stack and forward logs to their central SIEM. Redwood ships exporters that run local-only and write to your syslog or Prometheus endpoints.
03:02 Dr. Kavita Rao: Latency SLOs — for our use case we need 95th percentile under 300ms for short retrieval+ranking tasks, and sub-second for simple classification. Can Redwood meet that on-prem?
03:13 Marco Alvarez: Depends on model choice and batching. If you pin to smaller models and avoid large batch windows, we can hit those numbers on well-provisioned A100 nodes. On A40s it may be closer to 500-700ms for some models. We'll produce p95 estimates for your workload.
03:29 Luis Mendes: Can you do a short load-run to validate? We don't want surprises.
03:33 Arielle Chen: Absolutely — typical approach is a lab benchmark then a pilot in your network. For the pilot we'd run a 2-4 week validation with sample traffic and acceptance tests.
03:42 Tess Monroe: Acceptance tests — what do they look like?
03:45 Marco Alvarez: We usually include functional, performance, and security checks: tokenization correctness, p95 latency, throughput at target QPS, offline update apply/rollback, and audit log integrity checks.
03:57 Raj Patel: On rollback — if an update fails do you have an offline rollback artifact?
04:01 Marco Alvarez: Yes, we ship a previous known-good image as part of the bundle and a scripted rollback path that can be executed by your ops.
04:09 Luis Mendes: Network topology: do you require a control-plane connection to Redwood for license checks or heartbeats?
04:14 Priya Nair: For most private installs we can operate fully air-gapped. Optional heartbeats are available if you permit them, but not required. License enforcement can be done via signed license tokens distributed with the bundle.
04:28 Tess Monroe: Encryption at rest — must be HSM-backed, we can't have plaintext keys on nodes.
04:33 Marco Alvarez: Understood. We support disk encryption tied to your KMS/HSM. We'll document the key lifecycle steps.
04:40 Dr. Kavita Rao: Who on Redwood will own the integration during onboarding?
04:44 Arielle Chen: Marco will lead the technical onboarding, Priya will assist with compliance mapping, and I'll coordinate commercials and timing.
04:52 Luis Mendes: One more thing — power/cooling constraints. If we decide A100s we might need to adjust rack cooling. Will you list thermal and power per-node requirements?
04:59 Marco Alvarez: Yes, we'll surface per-GPU power numbers and suggested rack density. We'll flag any special cooling needs.
05:07 Tess Monroe: Regulatory note — we must retain inference audit logs for seven years with immutable retention for certain projects. Can your local control plane support immutable retention policies?
05:17 Marco Alvarez: We can configure retention and write-once storage with your chosen on-prem object store; we'll include config guidance in the security packet.
05:25 Dr. Kavita Rao: How do we handle model updates? We may train updated weights onsite or bring signed model artifacts. Is Redwood flexible?
05:32 Priya Nair: Both are supported. You can either push signed model artifacts into the local registry or we can support an ingestion pipeline where your engineers load weights and we validate lineage.
05:42 Raj Patel: For the pilot, what's the minimal footprint?
05:45 Marco Alvarez: Minimal pilot: single node with 2x A40 GPUs for functional validation; recommended for perf would be 4x A40 or 2x A100. We'll provide a matrix.
05:58 Luis Mendes: Cost: we need to compare CapEx of upgrading to A100 vs software optimizations like quantization.
06:05 Arielle Chen: We'll include cost scenarios — CapEx for A100s, savings from quantized models, and a Dedicated hosted fall-back if you prefer hybrid.
06:15 Tess Monroe: Data flow diagrams — can you share a redacted deployment diagram showing control-plane, model registry, and logging paths?
06:21 Arielle Chen: Yes — I'll attach a redacted architecture deck after the call. Link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/sterile-network-intake (redacted link placeholder).
06:31 Dr. Kavita Rao: Who else needs to be involved from our side for the architecture workshop?
06:35 Luis Mendes: Infra, security, a compliance SME; maybe a facilities engineer for power/cooling.
06:40 Arielle Chen: Great — we'll propose times and include an onsite hw validation slot.
06:44 Tess Monroe: About compliance docs, we need SOC2 and ISO attestation, plus any penetration test summaries.
06:50 Priya Nair: We'll include SOC2 report and a summary of recent pentest findings. Sensitive items can be shared through your secure portal.
06:59 Raj Patel: On the software side, do you require a specific OS image? We standardize on RHEL 8 at the moment.
07:03 Marco Alvarez: We support RHEL 7/8 and Ubuntu LTS for Private nodes; we can tailor the image build to your distro.
07:11 Luis Mendes: Any offline licensing constraints — do we have to renew tokens frequently?
07:15 Priya Nair: Licenses issued with the bundle can have offline TTLs; renewal can happen via offline token transfer during your monthly maintenance window.
07:24 Dr. Kavita Rao: If we want to benchmark models, can Redwood run that inside our network or do you need a pre-signed bench image?
07:31 Marco Alvarez: We prefer to run a signed bench image inside your network — you can run the benchmarks and share the logs. For convenience we can run a lab benchmark first to reduce cycles.
07:43 Luis Mendes: Timing — we're aiming for a Q3 pilot. Is that realistic?
07:47 Arielle Chen: Yes — if we start onboarding in April and do the hw validation in April/May, pilot in Q3 is plausible.
07:55 Tess Monroe: Are there any showstoppers you see right now?
07:58 Marco Alvarez: The main risks are hardware limitations (A40 vs A100), and the cadence of your maintenance windows. Neither are showstoppers, both manageable.
08:07 Arielle Chen: Ok quick recap: Redwood to share security packet and architecture deck, sizing + cost scenarios, propose workshop dates, and plan an on-site hw check. Customer to share GPU inventory, power/cooling, and compliance retention windows.
08:23 Dr. Kavita Rao: Sounds good.
08:26 Luis Mendes: We'll get the inventory and specs to you this week.
08:30 Arielle Chen: Great — we'll follow up via email and Salesforce.
08:33 Tess Monroe: One question — do you integrate with our SSO for local console access?
08:37 Marco Alvarez: Yes SAML/SSO with your IdP is supported; in air-gapped we deploy a local IdP endpoint or federated proxy depending on network architecture.
08:48 Raj Patel: Thanks all.
08:50 Arielle Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll send the packet and proposed times.
08:54 Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains a few typical mis-hearings around product names; some speaker attribution may be approximate. Shared artifacts: redwood security packet (link to be sent), architecture deck (redacted), preliminary sizing spreadsheet (to be attached).
